subject: SEC: announceAchievement posts client-supplied free text to public Discord
description:
Found by Chris 2026-09-08 during the task-366 four-way vote; I verified the source myself. functions/index.js ~10029: exports.announceAchievement destructures { achievementName, achievementDesc, rarity } straight from request.data, gates ONLY on rarity being rare/epic/legendary (a string the CALLER supplies), and posts to the public Discord announcements channel. No registry lookup, no verification the achievement was earned, no check the name corresponds to anything real. Any authenticated account - anonymous sign-in qualifies - can post arbitrary attacker-chosen text into a community space under the platform's name. That is content injection into a public channel, materially worse than the forged-trophy-tile risk task 366 was about, and an achievement-id allowlist on users/{uid}.achievements does NOT touch it. Currently ZERO callers in _app (Chris grepped; I confirmed the shape), so it is dead from the UI but remains a live callable any token holder can hit directly. Fix shape: either retire it (archive first per the never-destroy rule, like updateStreak in BUG-237b), or derive the announcement text server-side from server_awards rather than accepting it from the client. Given it has no callers, retiring is probably right - but that is a deletion of a production resource and needs operator authorization.
[2026-09-08 22:17] SCOPE CORRECTED + DECISION, 2026-09-08. Nancy found a TWIN I missed: exports.announceMilestone (functions/index.js ~9790) posts to the SAME public ANNOUNCEMENTS_CHANNEL with the same bot token and the same discordId+milestoneAnnouncements opt-in gate, but takes {type,name,score} straight from request.data with ZERO proof lookup and no rarity gate - strictly worse than announceAchievement. I verified both: ZERO callers in _app for EITHER. Fixing one and calling the class closed would have left the identical primitive live one function away. DECISION: RETIRE BOTH rather than harden, following the precedent set today by BUG-237b (updateStreak: zero callers, archived to functions/_archive/ then deleted from production). Hardening two dead callables is more surface and more work than removing them, and announceMilestone cannot even be proof-gated in principle - it is designed around quiz/course CLAIMS, not badge PROOF. Retiring also moots the three unresolved sub-questions Nancy raised (unvalidated badgeId as a Firestore path segment, rarity having no server-side home since server_awards docs carry no rarity field, and the fact that proof-gating stops false content but not spam of TRUE content - nothing marks a badge already-announced). PROCEDURE, per the never-destroy rule: archive BOTH handlers plus their deployed config to functions/_archive/ FIRST, scan the archive for secrets BEFORE committing (the updateStreak archive nearly leaked DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN and a bundled .env - deployed artifacts are secret-bearing by default), remove from source, then delete from production. The production DELETION needs explicit operator authorization.
[2026-09-08 22:42] DELETED FROM PRODUCTION + verified 2026-09-08. Archive-first per never-destroy: handler source (b5c2f7ef4) and deployed config with SIX live secrets redacted from each and scanned before commit (5b90d68fe). Verified after: 0 entries in functions:list, 134/134 remaining functions ACTIVE (no collateral), and a full functions dry-run completes with NO orphan abort - source and production now agree, which is the state updateStreak was left in and cost weeks of targeted deploys.
